poc.band_line: A pattern, plus obstruction of scrutiny and false statements to the public both proven, plus a repeat after an adverse finding.

ledger.type_name: Abuse of state power against people
ledger.elements: Bank accounts frozen (about 257) and protest powers used under a declaration the courts found had no lawful basis and breached the Charter. The declaration was cabinet's, announced by him.
ledger.headline: Invoked the Emergencies Act against the convoy protests and froze people's bank accounts. Two courts have ruled it was illegal. Nobody paid for it.

ledger.elements: The prime minister, his staff, the finance minister's office and the clerk pressed the attorney general over months to overrule the prosecution service on SNC-Lavalin — a decision reserved to her alone. Found by the commissioner.
ledger.headline: Leaned on his attorney general to spare SNC-Lavalin a criminal trial. Broke the ethics law. Two ministers who wouldn't go along were pushed out.

ledger.elements: A gift (the island stay, the helicopter) from a party whose foundation was registered to lobby his office with a $15-million grant pending; not refused. Found by the commissioner.
ledger.headline: Took a free holiday on a billionaire's private island while the billionaire's foundation lobbied his office. Broke the ethics law. Paid nothing.

ledger.elements: A benefit to his family (about $282,000 in fees from WE); WE had a $912-million programme before cabinet; he did not recuse — all admitted. Cleared because the Act's 'private interest' excludes relatives' fees.
ledger.note: Cleared under the Act, May 2021. The Supreme Court struck down the clause shielding that clearance in July 2026; the Federal Court of Appeal now reviews it.
ledger.headline: Handed a $912-million student program to a charity that had paid his mother and brother over $280,000 in speaking fees. Didn't recuse. Cleared, and now the courts get to check that.

ledger.elements: Publicly pre-judged (twice, on the record) a decision reserved to police and prosecutors. The statements are his; their effect was never examined by any body.
ledger.note: Counsel's claims that records were withheld and code names used were argued in court, not ruled on: not scored.
ledger.headline: His government prosecuted a vice-admiral for leaking, after Trudeau twice predicted the case would go to court before any charge existed. The case collapsed.

ledger.elements: Parliament twice ordered the records; the government withheld them and filed a Federal Court application against the Speaker. The agency president was formally admonished by the House. All of it on the record, by the government's own acts.
ledger.headline: Two scientists with ties to Chinese military researchers were fired from Canada's top-security lab. His government fought Parliament in court to keep the files secret.

ledger.elements: Free travel from WE; WE had a $912-million programme before the minister; no recusal. Found by the commissioner: preferential treatment, a decision in conflict, failure to recuse.
ledger.headline: Finance minister took free trips from WE, let his staff run interference for WE's funding, then helped hand WE a $912-million program. Broke the law three ways. Resigned.

ledger.type_name: Public money to insiders, or without the rules
ledger.elements: Some $60 million of public money went to contractors without the controls the rules require; in 76% of contracts people paid for did no work (procurement ombud). Found by the Auditor General.
ledger.headline: An app first estimated at $80,000 ended up costing about $60 million. A two-man firm got $19 million. Nobody has been charged.

ledger.type_name: Public money to insiders, or without the rules
ledger.elements: $209 million in contracts awarded with frequent disregard for the procurement rules. Found by the Auditor General.
ledger.headline: Federal contracts to McKinsey went from $2 million in the nine years before he took office to more than $100 million under him. The Auditor General found the rules were routinely ignored.

ledger.type_name: Public money to insiders, or without the rules
ledger.elements: A $4.5-million appointment went to a long-time family friend; the House voted 174–150 that he step aside. The friendship is on the record; the vote is Parliament's, not an adjudication.
ledger.headline: To head off a public inquiry into Chinese interference, he appointed a family friend and Trudeau Foundation member to review it. The House voted him out within three months.

ledger.type_name: Public money to insiders, or without the rules
ledger.elements: $76 million in 90 funding decisions where conflict-of-interest rules were not followed; $59 million to ineligible projects; the chair found in breach. Found by the Auditor General and the commissioner.
ledger.headline: The government's billion-dollar green-tech fund gave $59 million to ineligible projects and $76 million in deals where board members had conflicts. Parliament seized up for four months over the documents.

ledger.elements: The House ordered the documents; the government did not fully comply; the House sat on the privilege question for four months. On the record.
ledger.headline: The government's billion-dollar green-tech fund gave $59 million to ineligible projects and $76 million in deals where board members had conflicts. Parliament seized up for four months over the documents.

ledger.headline: Trade minister gave $23,000 in contracts to her friend's PR firm. Broke the ethics law. Kept her job.

cases.headline: Promised to end every long-term boil-water advisory on reserves within five years. The deadline passed with 58 still in place.

consequence.what: Nobody. The minister restated the commitment and set no date.

posture.what: 'Remains firm' — the deadline missed that month; no new date. Minimized.

change.what: More money pledged; the funding formula the Auditor General flagged was left as it was.

cases.poc_note: A missed commitment. No private benefit, no false statement, no rule broken: not corruption.

cases.poc_note: A fiscal outcome. Not corruption unless the promise was made knowing it would not be kept; the record does not show that.

change.what: Two more written commitments missed after this one: the balanced budget, the water advisories.

cases.poc_note: A broken promise, not a false statement of fact. Not corruption.

consequence.name: Consequence
consequence.line: What landed on the person responsible, in office.

rubric.1: On the leader personally: resigned over it, fined, sanctioned, repaid, or his own decision reversed under pressure.
rubric.0.5: On the responsible minister or official: resigned or removed over it, sanctioned; or the specific decision reversed.
rubric.0: Nothing. Words are nothing: an apology, 'accepting' a report, a review ordered, a recommendation accepted. Money paid by the treasury is nothing. Anything after leaving office is nothing.

posture.name: Posture
posture.line: What he did with it before a body ruled.

rubric.owned: Admitted it or acted on it before any finding, and did not obstruct.
rubric.nothing: Said nothing of substance, or accepted the finding only once it was made.
rubric.fought: Denied, minimized, blamed others, appealed, litigated, withheld records, invoked cabinet confidence, prorogued, or refused an order.

change.name: Change
change.line: Whether anything actually changed, in office.

rubric.1: A law, a rule, a process or a decision changed, and the conduct did not recur.
rubric.0: Nothing changed; a change promised, accepted or 'under implementation'; the same conduct recurred; or the change came after leaving office.

definitions.oa_owed: A body found against the leader, the government or a minister, or they admitted the fault. Cleared, upheld, never-examined and cost-only cases are out: neither for nor against.
definitions.oa_time: Nothing after the last day in office counts. Owning it counts only before the finding. Cooperating with a process the law requires is not owning it.

oa_bands.name: Fully accountable
oa_bands.line: Owned it, paid for it, changed it, in office.

oa_bands.name: Accountable
oa_bands.line: Most findings owned before they were forced; consequences borne at the top; rules changed in office.

oa_bands.name: Partly accountable
oa_bands.line: Some consequences borne at the top; some findings owned before they were forced; some rules changed.

oa_bands.name: Others paid
oa_bands.line: Consequences fell on ministers and officials, not on him. More findings fought than owned. Little changed.

oa_bands.name: Unaccountable
oa_bands.line: Fought or ignored the findings. Nothing landed on him. The same conduct again.

T1.name: Self-dealing and conflicts
elements: a benefit — a gift, money, travel, a contract, a licence, a programme — to the office-holder, their family, their party, or a close associate
the giver or recipient had, or sought, business with the government
the office-holder did not refuse it, or did not recuse from the decision

T2.name: Interference with an independent process
elements: the office-holder or their office intervened in, pressured, or publicly pre-judged
a decision reserved to an independent actor: a prosecutor, a judge, the police, an officer of Parliament, an arm's-length appointment
without lawful authority to direct that decision

T3.name: Abuse of state power against people
elements: state power was used against people: detention, property, bank accounts, prosecution, surveillance
a court found the legal conditions for using it were not met, or that it breached their rights

T4.name: Public money to insiders, or without the rules
elements: public funds, contracts, grants or appointments went
to insiders, friends, party-connected people, ineligible recipients, or without the controls the rules require
as found by an auditor, an officer of Parliament, a court, a recorded vote of Parliament, or admitted — beyond ordinary error

T5.name: False statements to the public
elements: a public statement of fact by the office-holder, their office, or a minister
contradicted by a document, a finding, or their own later statement on the record
about a matter they were in a position to know

T6.name: Obstruction of scrutiny
elements: an investigator, a committee, a court, an inquiry, or Parliament sought records or answers
the office-holder or government withheld them, redacted beyond the order, ended the process (prorogation, a confidence vote, dissolution), or went to court against disclosure
as shown by an order, a ruling, a formal admonishment, or the record

T7.name: Breach of their own written standard
elements: a written standard the office-holder set, signed, or swore to
was broken, per a finding or an admission
with none of the types above present

E4.name: Adjudicated
E4.meaning: A court, an officer of Parliament, an auditor, or a public inquiry found it.

E3.name: Admitted / own record
E3.meaning: They admitted it, or it is their own act or document on the record: a settlement paid, a lawsuit filed, an itinerary issued, a statement made.

E2.name: Documented, no ruling
E2.meaning: On the public record — sworn testimony, released documents, a recorded vote of the House — but no body with authority ruled on it.

E1.name: Reported, never examined
E1.meaning: Reported by major outlets, denied or unanswered, examined by nobody. Listed. Scores nothing.

him.name: The leader personally: his own act or statement, or a decision he announced and defended as his own

office.name: His staff, or a cabinet decision carried by a minister

government.name: A department, agency or body under the government

severity.rule: S = 1 + [harm or ≥$10M public money] + [a body found against them], capped at 3

poc_bands.name: None
poc_bands.test: No proven corrupt act on the record.

poc_bands.name: Isolated
poc_bands.test: Proven acts, none by the leader personally.

poc_bands.name: Repeated
poc_bands.test: More than one proven act by the leader personally, or one by the leader and three or more across the government.

poc_bands.name: Pattern
poc_bands.test: Proven acts by the leader personally in three or more types, or the same type again after an adverse finding.

poc_bands.name: Systemic
poc_bands.test: A pattern, plus obstruction of scrutiny and false statements to the public both proven, plus a repeat after an adverse finding.
